answer: A cheap defence is to make identity expensive in time rather than in money. Each answer a node writes is sealed by four peers and dated against the previous close, so a trellis of accounts has to wait a real epoch between each rung; a grove of clones can be sprouted in one night but none of them carries history. The canyon is the narrow quorum gate: duplicate rows echo back as 409, so copying an honest answer buys nothing and only slows the copier down.
